req.title: Update requires title
req.statement: The system shall render 'Title is required.' when POST /<id>/update omits the title.

doc.reasoning: R-FLASKR-018 requires that POST /<id>/update with a missing title renders 'Title is required.' and returns HTTP 2xx. Three tests are designed: (1) positive — valid update with title succeeds and redirects (EP, confirms the non-error path so mutations to the error branch are caught); (2) negative — POST with empty title string returns 2xx and contains exact error text (NEG + EP, catches string-mutation and condition-flip mutations); (3) boundary — POST with title='' (zero-length, the exact boundary) vs title=' ' (one space, non-empty) to catch off-by-one / truthiness mutations on the `if not title` guard (BVA). All tests use pre-loaded data: post id=2 belongs to user Rahul (id=1), so we log in as Rahul. Assertions use exact status codes and exact byte strings to maximise mutation kill rate.

tests.name: test_update_with_valid_title_redirects
preconditions: Database contains pre-loaded rows (user id=1 Rahul, post id=2 author_id=1)
User Rahul is logged in via POST /auth/login
Post id=2 exists and belongs to Rahul
actions: POST /2/update with title='Updated Title', body='Updated body'
expected: Response does NOT contain 'Title is required.'
trace: R-FLASKR-018: positive path — title present, no error rendered
Catches mutations that flip the `if not title` condition to always-true
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app

fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp()
os.close(fd)
app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})

with app.app_context():
    from flaskr.db import init_db
    init_db()

client = app.test_client()

# Log in as Rahul (author of post id=2)
r = client.post('/auth/login', data={'username': 'Rahul', 'password': 'stone'})
assert r.status_code == 302, f'Login failed: {r.status_code}'

# POST update with a valid non-empty title
r = client.post('/2/update', data={'title': 'Updated Title', 'body': 'Updated body'})
assert r.status_code == 302, f'Expected 302 redirect, got {r.status_code}'
assert r.headers['Location'] == '/', f'Unexpected redirect: {r.headers.get("Location")}'
assert b'Title is required.' not in r.data

os.unlink(path)

tests.name: test_update_title_boundary_empty_vs_single_space
preconditions: Database contains pre-loaded rows (user id=1 Rahul, post id=2 author_id=1)
User Rahul is logged in via POST /auth/login
actions: POST /2/update with title='' (zero-length — boundary at falsy)
POST /2/update with title=' ' (one space — boundary at truthy)
expected: title='' (empty): HTTP 200 with 'Title is required.' in body
title=' ' (single space): HTTP 302 redirect (no error, space is truthy in Python)
trace: R-FLASKR-018: BVA on the `if not title` guard
Catches off-by-one / truthiness mutations: `not title` vs `len(title) == 0` vs `title is None`
Catches mutations that change the boundary condition direction

import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app

fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp()
os.close(fd)
app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})

with app.app_context():
    from flaskr.db import init_db
    init_db()

client = app.test_client()

# Log in as Rahul (author of post id=2)
r = client.post('/auth/login', data={'username': 'Rahul', 'password': 'stone'})
assert r.status_code == 302, f'Login failed: {r.status_code}'

# Boundary: title is exactly empty string (falsy) — must show error
r_empty = client.post('/2/update', data={'title': '', 'body': 'body text'})
assert r_empty.status_code == 200, f'Expected 200 for empty title, got {r_empty.status_code}'
assert b'Title is required.' in r_empty.data, 'Error message missing for empty title'

# Boundary: title is a single space (truthy in Python) — must NOT show error
r_space = client.post('/2/update', data={'title': ' ', 'body': 'body text'})
assert r_space.status_code == 302, f'Expected 302 for space title, got {r_space.status_code}'
assert b'Title is required.' not in r_space.data, 'Unexpected error for single-space title'
assert r_space.headers['Location'] == '/', f'Unexpected redirect: {r_space.headers.get("Location")}'

os.unlink(path)
